markets.rules_primary: If the Bank of England takes the action of Cut more than 25bps at December Monetary Policy Committee meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The market resolves based on the official policy rate decision announced by the central bank. For central banks with multiple policy rates, only changes to the primary policy rate count. If the meeting is cancelled or delayed past the expiration date, markets for "No change" resolve to Yes and all others resolve to No. Emergency rate changes between scheduled meetings do not affect resolution of contracts tied to scheduled meetings. The specific basis point ranges are inclusive (e.g., "25-50bp" includes both 25bp and 50bp changes).

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire when election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If the certified percentage of the popular vote received by Vox in the 2026 Spanish general election is 13% to 100%, inclusive of both endpoints, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The percentage is the share of the vote received by Vox in the election to the Congress of Deputies. It is calculated as (total votes received by the specified person/party ÷ total valid votes cast) × 100, rounded to two decimal places.

Resolution uses the official results published by the Spanish Ministry of the Interior as proclaimed by the Junta Electoral Central, NOT the provisional count on election night
Only the election to the Congress of Deputies counts. Votes cast in the Senate election held the same day do NOT count
Invalid ballots are excluded from the denominator. Blank ballots are valid votes under Spanish electoral law and are included in the denominator, as in the official percentages
Votes for Vox include votes for any coalition or regional list the Ministry of the Interior aggregates under Vox in its national results
markets.title: Will Vox receive at least 13% of the popular vote in the 2026 Spanish general election?

markets.rules_primary: If the margin of victory for the People's Party in the 2026 Spanish general election is within 0% to 3%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The margin of victory is the share of valid votes received by the party named in the market minus the share received by the party that finishes second if the named party finishes first, or minus the share of the party that finishes first if the named party does not. If the named party finishes first, the margin will be positive; if it does not, the margin will be negative; if it ties for first place, the margin shall be 0. Vote shares are the nationwide percentages of valid votes (which in Spain include blank ballots) in the official Congress of Deputies results published by the Ministerio del Interior, under which votes for a party's regional affiliate lists (for example, PSC-PSOE for PSOE) count toward that party.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound, and no rounding shall be applied. For example, for consecutive ranges of 3-6% and 6-9%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 3-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-9% range.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if certified election results are published.
markets.rules_primary: If the People's Party finishes in 1st place in the CERA vote (Spaniards resident abroad) in the 2026 Spanish general election according to the certified results, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Ranking is determined by the specified counting method:
Rank is based on Congress of Deputies vote totals from CERA voters only
The CERA vote is the vote cast by electors in the Censo de Electores Residentes Ausentes (Spaniards resident abroad)
A party's CERA total is its Congress of Deputies vote total for residents abroad (CERA) published by the Spanish Ministry of the Interior (Infoelectoral). If the Ministry has not published that total when certified results are published, the sum of the party's CERA votes recorded by the Juntas Electorales Provinciales in the general scrutiny (escrutinio general), across all provinces, is used. Ranking uses these totals, regardless of the national result
Resolution follows the final certified general scrutiny, not the provisional count published on election night
Only the election to the Congress of Deputies counts. Senate votes do NOT count
Votes for a party's regional federation or joint list that runs under its name count toward that party (for example, votes for the Socialists' Party of Catalonia, PSC-PSOE, count toward the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party)
CERA ballots that are not included in the final certified general-scrutiny totals do NOT count

In case of exact ties, markets resolve proportionally (1/number of tied entities). Write-in candidates achieving the specified rank resolve all named candidate markets to NO unless a specific "Write-in" or "Other" option exists. Candidates who withdraw or are disqualified after the filing deadline but remain on the ballot are ranked based on votes received. If the election is cancelled or postponed beyond expiration, all markets resolve to NO.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Taco Bell Foot Traffic (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 89 , then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on finalized Carbon Arc values recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of the month covered by this market. For example, finalized Carbon Arc values for August will be recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7th.

The index measures year-over-year change, where 100 means Taco Bell Foot Traffic was equal to the same month last year. Values above 100 indicate growth and values below 100 indicate decline: for example, 103 = 3% more visits than year prior, 97 = 3% fewer visits than year prior. The index is measured by Carbon Arc mobile location data across 200M+ devices, matched to the same calendar days of the prior year and normalized for seasonality, weather, and holidays. The panel updates daily as new data arrives.

markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on the Carbon Arc Streaming Apps Array value for the full month covered by this market, as recorded by Kalshi at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of that month. For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7th. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Streaming Apps Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=4a5e14d8-0a48-449b-9733-5fadf6a45851&entity=Streaming+Apps. The underlying metric is app downloads. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Netflix, Hulu: Stream shows & movies, Disney+, Paramount+, Peacock TV: Stream TV & Movies, Max: Stream HBO, TV, & Movies, ESPN: Live Sports & Scores, each weighted 1/7. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured app downloads equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the underlying companies. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on finalized Carbon Arc values recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of the month covered by this market. For example, finalized Carbon Arc values for August will be recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7th.

The index measures year-over-year change, where 100 means Sweetgreen Foot Traffic was equal to the same month last year. The index is measured by Carbon Arc mobile location data across 200M+ devices, matched to the same calendar days of the prior year and normalized for seasonality, weather, and holidays. The panel updates daily as new data arrives.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Rideshare app downloads array index (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 80, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on the Carbon Arc Rideshare Apps Array value for the full month covered by this market, as recorded by Kalshi at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of that month. For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Rideshare Apps Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=2fff36c3-6355-4b68-a914-9bd5013f185a&entity=Rideshare+Apps. The underlying metric is app downloads. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Uber - Request a ride, Lyft, each weighted 1/2. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured app downloads equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on the Carbon Arc Rideshare Apps Array value for the full month covered by this market, as recorded by Kalshi at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of that month. For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Rideshare Apps Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=2fff36c3-6355-4b68-a914-9bd5013f185a&entity=Rideshare+Apps. The underlying metric is app downloads. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Uber - Request a ride, Lyft, each weighted 1/2. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured app downloads equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

markets.rules_primary: If the Carbon Arc Coffee chain foot traffic array index (November 2026) for November 2026 is above 97, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, determination will resolve on the Carbon Arc Coffee Chains Array value for the full month covered by this market, as recorded by Kalshi at 11:59 p.m. ET on the 7th calendar day after the end of that month. For example, the value for August is recorded at 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7. Later corrections or revisions will not affect the recorded value.

The reference is Carbon Arc's published full-month Coffee Chains Array level: https://www.carbonarc.co/prisms?prism=ca2222e8-3be0-4883-a103-96d37c4aeb76&entity=Coffee+Chains. The underlying metric is foot traffic. The array is the equally weighted arithmetic mean of its constituent year-over-year indices. At listing, its members are Dutch Bros. Coffee, Starbucks, each weighted 1/2. Each constituent index is 100 when its measured foot traffic equals the same month of the previous year; the array averages these indices. An array level of 103 means the constituents' average year-over-year growth is 3%, and 97 means their average decline is 3%.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the underlying companies. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If Tatiana has gained Michelin stars in the 2026 annual Michelin Guide compared with the prior annual edition, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Eligible restaurants have never held a Michelin star and had zero stars in the prior annual edition; any gain to one or more qualifies. Compare the official 2026 annual Michelin Guide with the 2025 annual edition. Use each restaurant's exact official name at the listed location; relocations are not tracked. Only the official publication for Dec 2026 is used; later revisions, retractions, and mid-year changes do not count. If a restaurant permanently closes before the new Guide is released and is not listed, its market resolves to No. Temporary closures or name changes do not count as a change unless Michelin attributes a different number of stars. Bib Gourmand, unstarred Guide inclusion, and Green Stars do not count as Michelin star gains. Each restaurant market resolves independently; multiple restaurants may resolve Yes.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Michelin Guide. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If the United States federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse of appropriations at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 12, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A shutdown is defined as the government's orderly suspension of agency work that is not legally excepted, typically accompanied by furloughing the employees who perform that work, when funding is unavailable.

Examples that would resolve the market to Yes:

OMB releases a formal directive that orders heads of the affected agencies to "execute plans for an orderly shutdown," which is in effect as of 10:00 AM ET on Dec 12, 2026
OPM posts a current operating status that indicates that "due to a partial lapse in appropriations, Federal Government operations vary by agency"

Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:

A technical lapse in appropriations occurs, but OMB directs agencies to continue standard operations
Government closures or operating status changes resulting from Federal holidays, inclement weather, or other emergencies, unless such closures coincide with a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If Steve Hilton's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 California governor election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 California governor election at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was Becerra 58.2%, Hilton 34.2% (Becerra +24.0), so Steve Hilton's polling margin is -24.0 points. Steve Hilton outperforms if the certified margin of victory is greater than -24.0 points.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.

markets.rules_secondary:
The Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 is the statute at Title I of Division N of Public Law 114-113 (6 U.S.C. 1501 et seq.), not the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Its authorities are in effect through December 11, 2026.

Legislation extends the Act if it postpones the date on which the Act ceases to have effect, or otherwise reauthorizes it, for any length of time. It counts whether it is enacted as a standalone bill or as a provision of a larger bill, such as a defense authorization, an appropriations act or a continuing resolution, and whether final passage comes on the bill itself, a conference report or a motion to concur.
